targets.authors: Damisch, L., Stoberock, B., & Mussweiler, T.
targets.title: Keep your fingers crossed! How superstition improves performance.
targets.evidence_quote: Here we report two high-powered, precise replications of the golf and superstition experiment (Study 1) from Damisch et al. (2010).
targets.outcome_quote: Our failure to replicate the target study was not due to lack of impact, lack of statistical power, differences in task difficulty, nor differences in participant belief in luck.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Both a close replication and a stronger manipulation failed to find the performance benefit; authors state an overall failed-replication verdict.

reasoning: Title, DOI and both authors verified on first page of seven-page article. Two new participant samples retest the 2010 golf experiment. Damisch dissertation, Lee and Aruguete works enter the literature review and meta-analysis but are not separately retested in the two new experiments, so are excluded as targets. Completed results, despite preregistration.
